natural: in line with Heaven and the people

meaning.en: To act in accord with the will of Heaven and the wishes of the people; used to justify a righteous cause.
meaning.zh: 顺应天命，适应民心，指行事合乎天意民心。

equivalents: accord with Heaven and the people

examples.zh: 这次改革顺天应人，得到了广泛支持。
examples.en: This reform accords with the people's wishes and won broad support.

examples.zh: 史书称他起兵是顺天应人之举。
examples.en: The histories call his uprising a righteous act in line with Heaven and the people.

story.en: The Yijing on revolution: 'Tang and Wu changed the mandate, obeying Heaven and responding to the people' (汤武革命，顺乎天而应乎人).
story.zh: 《周易·革·彖传》：“汤武革命，顺乎天而应乎人。”

date.zh: 西周至战国 · 前9—前3世纪
date.en: Western Zhou to Warring States, 9th–3rd c. BC

usage.en: Formal, positive; often in political or historical writing.
usage.zh: 正式，含褒义，多见于政治、历史文章。

meaning.en: To chatter idly, passing judgement on others and gossiping about right and wrong.
meaning.zh: 随意议论是非，信口评说。

examples.zh: 别在背后说白道黑，有意见当面提。
examples.en: Don't gossip behind people's backs; say it to their faces.

examples.zh: 他们几个爱说白道黑，对谁都有评论。
examples.en: The few of them love to gossip and have something to say on everyone.

usage.en: Casual, mildly critical; compare 说长道短 (the more common form).
usage.zh: 口语，略含批评，近“说长道短”（更常用）。

meaning.en: To chat about all sorts of topics, old and new.
meaning.zh: 谈论古今的各种事情，形容谈话内容广泛。

equivalents: talk about everything under the sun

examples.zh: 老人们坐在树下说古道今。
examples.en: The old folk sat under the tree and talked of days gone by and today.

examples.zh: 爷爷最爱和我们说古道今。
examples.en: Grandpa loves chatting to us about things old and new.

usage.en: Friendly, usually about leisurely conversation; neutral or warm.
usage.zh: 语气亲切，多指闲谈，中性或褒义。

meaning.en: So big that nothing compares to it.
meaning.zh: 大得没有可以相比的，形容极其巨大。

examples.zh: 展厅中央摆着一块硕大无朋的陨石。
examples.en: A colossal meteorite stood in the middle of the hall.

examples.zh: 这棵硕大无朋的古树已有千年。
examples.en: This colossal old tree is a thousand years old.

story.en: The Book of Songs praises a man: 'That person, big beyond compare' (彼其之子，硕大无朋).
story.zh: 《诗经·唐风·椒聊》：“彼其之子，硕大无朋。”

date.zh: 西周初至春秋中叶 · 前11—前6世纪
date.en: early Western Zhou to mid Spring and Autumn, 11th–6th c. BC

usage.en: Used of physical size; 硕 reads shuò. Don't use of abstract things.
usage.zh: 形容体积，“硕”读 shuò，不用于抽象事物。

meaning.zh: 为个人打算的想法和各种杂乱的念头。

examples.zh: 干部要摒除私心杂念，一心为民。
examples.en: Officials should rid themselves of selfish motives and serve the people.

examples.zh: 考试时要排除私心杂念，专心答题。
examples.en: During an exam, clear your mind of stray thoughts and focus.

usage.en: Often as the object of 摒除/排除/抛开; can be selfishness or just mental clutter.
usage.zh: 多作“摒除”“排除”的宾语，可指自私念头，也可指杂念。

meaning.en: Ideas flowing abundantly and swiftly, especially in writing.
meaning.zh: 思路像泉水涌出一样，形容文思敏捷、灵感不断。

examples.zh: 他提笔写作时思如泉涌，一夜写了三章。
examples.en: When he writes, ideas pour out of him; he wrote three chapters in one night.

examples.zh: 讨论会上大家思如泉涌，想出了很多点子。
examples.en: At the brainstorm everyone's ideas flowed and many proposals came up.

usage.en: Positive; used of writers and creative work. Compare 文思泉涌.
usage.zh: 褒义，多用于写作和创意，可比较“文思泉涌”。

meaning.en: To pester or harass someone persistently and shamelessly until they give in.
meaning.zh: 纠缠不休，不顾对方意愿地一再纠缠。

examples.zh: 他对她死缠烂打，她反而更讨厌他了。
examples.en: He pestered her relentlessly, and she only came to dislike him more.

examples.zh: 推销员死缠烂打，客户赶紧挂了电话。
examples.en: The salesman badgered on, and the client hung up quickly.

usage.en: Colloquial and derogatory; used in courtship, sales, disputes.
usage.zh: 口语，贬义，用于追求、推销、争执等场合。

meaning.en: To think very hard, especially to come up with writing or ideas.
meaning.zh: 形容竭力思索，多指苦思文句。

examples.zh: 他搜索枯肠，也想不出合适的标题。
examples.en: He racked his brains but couldn't come up with a suitable title.

examples.zh: 为了这首诗，诗人搜索枯肠了好几天。
examples.en: For this poem, the poet racked his brains for days.

origin.source: 卢仝《走笔谢孟谏议寄新茶》

story.en: Lu Tong's poem on tea: 'The third bowl searches my dry bowels, leaving only five thousand scrolls of writing' (三碗搜枯肠，唯有文字五千卷).
story.zh: 卢仝《走笔谢孟谏议寄新茶》：“三碗搜枯肠，唯有文字五千卷。”

usage.en: Used of writing and creative thinking; compare 绞尽脑汁 (broader).
usage.zh: 多用于写作和构思，范围比“绞尽脑汁”窄。

meaning.en: A plain carriage with white horses, used for funerals; mourning.
meaning.zh: 白色的车马，旧时用于丧事，表示吊唁或哀悼。

examples.zh: 葬礼上，亲友们素车白马，送别老人。
examples.en: At the funeral relatives and friends, in mourning, saw the old man off.

examples.zh: 诗中写他素车白马赶来奔丧。
examples.en: The poem tells of him rushing to the funeral with a white carriage and horses.

usage.en: Literary; only for funerals. Not used for weddings.
usage.zh: 书面语，只用于丧事，不用于喜事。

natural: hold the sword by the blade

meaning.en: To hand weapon or power to others, so that one is in danger; to lose control of one's own power.
meaning.zh: 把剑柄交给别人，自己握着剑刃，比喻把大权交给别人，自己反受其害。

examples.zh: 把核心技术交给对方，等于太阿倒持。
examples.en: Giving the key technology to the other side is like handing them the sword.

examples.zh: 君主大权旁落，是太阿倒持的下场。
examples.en: A ruler who loses power has handed over the sword and suffers for it.

story.en: Mei Fu warned the emperor: 'To hold the Tai'e sword upside down and hand its hilt to another' (倒持太阿，授楚其柄).
story.zh: 《汉书·梅福传》：“倒持太阿，授楚其柄。”

usage.en: Literary; 太阿 is the name of a famous sword; read ē. Do not confuse with 授人以柄 (which is milder).
usage.zh: 书面语，“太阿”为古代名剑，读 ē，与较轻的“授人以柄”有别。

meaning.en: Broad and level like a whetstone; also, a smooth road, a wide-open path.
meaning.zh: 像磨刀石一样平坦宽广，形容道路平坦，也比喻前途顺利。

examples.zh: 高速公路坦荡如砥，开车十分轻松。
examples.en: The motorway is broad and smooth and driving is easy.

examples.zh: 他的仕途并非坦荡如砥，经历过不少起伏。
examples.en: His career was not smooth sailing and had its ups and downs.

usage.en: Describes roads or prospects; 砥 reads dǐ. Not for people's character (use 光明磊落).
usage.zh: 形容道路或前途，“砥”读 dǐ。不用于形容人品（人品用“光明磊落”）。

meaning.en: Originally a TCM illness with confused mind; now, to be bewitched by an idea and act foolishly.
meaning.zh: 原为中医所称痰阻心窍、神志不清的病症，现多指被某种念头迷住而做出糊涂事。

examples.zh: 他像痰迷心窍似的，把全部积蓄都投了进去。
examples.en: As if he'd lost his head, he put all his savings into it.

examples.zh: 你是不是痰迷心窍，怎么会信这种骗局？
examples.en: Have you lost your senses? How could you believe such a scam?

usage.en: Casual and teasing or angry; 窍 reads qiào.
usage.zh: 口语，带嘲讽或恼怒语气，“窍”读 qiào。

meaning.en: To expose the chest and back; dressing in a revealing, sometimes improper way.
meaning.zh: 敞开胸脯，露出脊背，指穿着暴露。

examples.zh: 学校要求学生不得袒胸露背进入课堂。
examples.en: The school requires students not to come to class in revealing clothes.

examples.zh: 夏天街头有人袒胸露背，有碍观瞻。
examples.en: In summer some people go around half-naked, which looks unseemly.

usage.en: Mostly critical, about the occasion's decorum; neutral for sport or hot weather.
usage.zh: 多含批评，指场合不得体；也可中性描述天热时的穿着。

meaning.en: To let things develop naturally without interfering.
meaning.zh: 听任事物自然发展，不去干预。

examples.zh: 既然劝不动他，就听其自然吧。
examples.en: Since we can't talk him round, let things take their course.

examples.zh: 花草不必管得太细，听其自然就好。
examples.en: Plants don't need much fussing; just let them grow.

usage.en: Neutral; can sound relaxed or passive. Often as 只好听其自然.
usage.zh: 中性，可显洒脱，也可显消极，常作“只好听其自然”。

meaning.en: To slack off and play sly tricks to avoid work or gain advantage.
meaning.zh: 耍小聪明，不老实干活，想方设法占便宜。

examples.zh: 他干活总爱偷奸耍滑，同事们都不愿和他搭档。
examples.en: He always slacks and plays tricks at work, so colleagues don't want to team with him.

examples.zh: 做生意不能偷奸耍滑，要诚信。
examples.en: In business you can't cheat; you need integrity.

usage.zh: 口语，贬义，多指干活的人、做买卖的人。

natural: a fish that can swallow a boat

meaning.en: A huge fish that can swallow a boat; a great person or a major criminal.
meaning.zh: 能吞下船的大鱼，比喻大人物或重大罪犯。

equivalents: a great whale of a man

examples.zh: 严惩小贪容易，抓住吞舟之鱼才见力度。
examples.en: Punishing small bribes is easy; catching the big fish shows resolve.

examples.zh: 池塘养不出吞舟之鱼。
examples.en: A pond can't raise a fish that swallows boats.

story.en: Zhuangzi: 'A fish large enough to swallow a boat, when stranded out of water, is troubled even by ants' (吞舟之鱼，砀而失水，则蚁能苦之).
story.zh: 《庄子·庚桑楚》：“吞舟之鱼，砀而失水，则蚁能苦之。”

date.zh: 战国中期 · 前4—前3世纪

usage.en: Neutral/literary; the sense depends on context (a great man or a big criminal). 吞 reads tūn.
usage.zh: 文言色彩，依语境指大人物或首恶。

natural: cut flesh to patch a sore

meaning.en: To cut away good flesh to cover a sore: a short-term fix that does greater harm.
meaning.zh: 剜下好肉去补伤口，比喻只顾眼前，用有害的办法应急。

equivalents: a cure worse than the disease

examples.zh: 借新债还旧债，无异于挖肉补疮。
examples.en: Borrowing to repay old debts is like robbing Peter to pay Paul.

examples.zh: 砍树卖钱救急，不过是挖肉补疮。
examples.en: Cutting down trees to raise cash is only a self-defeating quick fix.

usage.en: Describes self-harming stopgap measures. Also written 剜肉补疮 (剜 wān, the older form). Compare 饮鸩止渴.
usage.zh: 指损害自己的权宜之计，也作“剜肉补疮”，近“饮鸩止渴”。
